title: 1.2 From Chips to Thoughts: Building Physical Intelligence into Robotic Systems
problem: Generative AI deployment in robotics and edge systems faces high energy costs for both training and inference on large multi-modal models, constraining real-time autonomous system deployment.
motivation: AI-driven robotics requires physical intelligence that integrates perception, reasoning, and control in energy-constrained embedded environments while maintaining generative AI capabilities.
method: The approach redesigns chips and system power management so robots can run large AI models directly on their hardware. It achieves this by integrating the AI tightly with sensors and motors—so sensor data flows immediately to the AI, which produces motor commands in real time—and by powering down unused components at each moment instead of running everything constantly.
key_novelty: Designing hardware so robots can run large generative AI models directly with integrated sensor-motor control, solving the energy-efficiency problem that prevents edge deployment.
contributions: Framework for deploying generative AI on robotic systems with energy constraints
Emphasis on physical intelligence as integration of perception, reasoning, and control
System-level approach from chip design to robotic deployment
Identification of energy efficiency as critical bottleneck for democratizing AI robotics
limitations: Not discussed; abstract is position paper style.
primary_theme: energy-efficient AI for robotic physical intelligence
